correctness.rationale: The quotient metric identity d(y,Gf(x))=min_g d(y,g f(x))=dbar(pi y,T pi x) is exact even with fixed points. Any lifts of a genuine quotient orbit are genuine F orbits. For periodic pseudo-orbits of period n and shadowing quotient orbit period m, repeat a nearest-lift block of length lcm(m,n), proving closure without changing tolerances. Induction gives F^n(x)=pi^{-1}(T^n pi x). For a free action compactness gives a positive minimal separation for distinct points in a fibre. For the nonfree two-sheet binary shift wedge, paired non-branch points tend to the branch point and can choose coincident successors; P_n=2(2^n-1)+1. These are arguments valid for all parameters, not consequences of finite n checks.
risk: Positive expansivity uses the explicitly specified all-pairs-of-multivalued-orbits definition; it should not be conflated with a uniqueness-of-trajectory convention.
Point-count zeta counts states admitting n-step return, not all multivalued paths.
